title: The Empty Waltz
sections: intro(0.0-7.5s) A(7.5-37.5s) B(37.5-67.5s) interlude(67.5-75.0s) A'(75.0-105.0s) coda(105.0-125.1s) (ends; natural decay tail)
instruments: harpsichord-like (8' + 4' and lute stop, KS quill strings), celesta, muted low strings (con sordino section + cello counter-line), pizzicato bass, soft clock ticks (interlude)
motif_notes: Head motif: rest on the downbeat, then 5th-octave (E5 A5) falling through the leading tone G#5-F5-E5: the waltz whose melody always enters after the downbeat (a missing partner). Those five pitches are the house 'For Krystal' shape in minor (5-1-7-b6-5, the same degrees as music_boss's A D C# Bb A), used deliberately as a family link but in a new rhythm, register and timbre; the rest of the tune is new. Lament bass A-G#-G-F(#). B section is a new flowing tune in C major rising to E6. Manor timbre (harpsichord/celesta/muted strings) is shared with m21.

title: A Midnight Invitation
key: E minor (Waltz II in G major, middle section in G minor)
instruments: velvet fiddle (solo bowed string), harpsichord (flourishes, Waltz II tune, running 8ths), muted string 'pah-pah', pizzicato bass, timpani, low bell (12 midnight strokes), frame drum, horn (from the existing boss piece), celesta, cymbal-air swell
motif_notes: Waltz I 'invitation': B4 leaps a minor sixth to G5 then leans down chromatically F#-E-D#. Waltz II: charming G-major tune with a C minor-6 shadow. MIDNIGHT: G-minor half-note theme in hemiola (2 against 3) in low strings, then fiddle, with twelve bell strokes; B3 climax reuses the minor-sixth leap on Eb/Dm/Cm.
location_playlist: Count Velour encounter (boss); MIDNIGHT section usable as phase-2 contrast

title: Harvest Trouble
key: C minor (B section E-flat major, bridge on a G pedal with a D-flat Neapolitan build)
instruments: spiccato muted strings doubled by a hard-mallet marimba (lead), cellos (B tune, A'' doubling), violins (B' tune two octaves up), pizzicato bass, muted-string stabs on 2 and 4, bones/clacks, brush, woodblock, frame drum, metal ticks, timpani and one low bell (bridge)
motif_notes: Scamper: C5-Eb5-G5-Eb5-C5 . G4 tumbling back, then a chromatic creep Ab4-B4-C5-D5-Eb5 and a b9 (Ab over G7); the answer turns to a D-flat (Neapolitan) bar. B: a legato cello song in E-flat with a G-major 'trouble' chord. Bridge: strings creep G-Ab-G-F# / Ab-Bb-Ab-G ... on a G-G-G-Ab pizzicato pedal while the marimba answers from above, a D-flat build with timpani roll, stop-time G7(b9) hits and ticks in the silence. Review rewrite: the first version (6/8 C-minor reed jig over marimba, ~68 s) shared meter, pulse, length and palette with m10 'Thorns in the Path' (6/8 E-minor oboe/bassoon over marimba, 67 s); this one is a 4/4 galop at 160 with a string/marimba lead. Distinct from the bosses: no toms or ostinato pluck, no Krystal motif, not 3/4.
location_playlist: Ordinary Chapter Two combat (orchard, commons, manor grounds)

New: 4/4 straight-eighth galop at 160, spiccato strings + hard-mallet marimba lead, cello B tune, same key, same E-flat contrast and G-pedal bridge idea. title: The Borrowed Welcome
key: B minor (tritone from the title's F major)
sections: S1(0.0-35.6s) S2 (canon at the tritone)(35.6-71.1s) S3 stretto(71.1-106.7s)
instruments: l1: wordless formant choir, music box (detuned), heartbeat, muted low strings, soft bass; l2: pizzicato 3+3+2 ostinato, frame drums, low bell, metal ticks, timpani; l3: horns (existing boss horn voice) in canon, high strings, choir descant, timpani rolls, air swells
motif_notes: Borrows the 'For Krystal' motif SHAPE (rising 4th + three steps down) in B minor: F#4 B4 A#4 G#4 F#4 (natural-minor turn F# B A G F# over G/C bars), and sets it against the motif at its original title pitches C5 F5 E5 D5 C5 (music box ~20-30 cents flat; second horn two beats behind the first = stretto canon) a tritone apart, over F/B - familiar intervals as unsettling counterpoint. Choir is wordless (formant vowels).
